set.body:
Objective:
Provide a Parquet source and sink through Frame source capabilities while preserving the distinction between lazy column-data scanning and effectful footer/schema inspection.

Scope:
- Open or inspect reads metadata and returns a structured source result; column pages remain lazy until execution.
- Projection, predicate, limit, row-group statistics, and partition pruning are negotiated explicitly and reported as accepted or residual.
- Decoding produces Frame Arrow-compatible batches. It is never described as memory-identical or universally zero-copy.
- JVM support may land first. A browser implementation is a separate platform adapter sharing schemas, fixtures, and capability semantics rather than sharing JVM code.
- Nested, decimal, timestamp, dictionary, and extension-type mappings use explicit compatibility tables and typed unsupported cases.

Acceptance:
- Deterministic Parquet fixtures round-trip required and nullable primitive, UTF-8, timestamp, and dictionary columns.
- Projection and predicate pushdown prove reduced row-group or column reads through receipts, not only result equality.
- Schema evolution, missing fields, coercion, corrupt metadata, unsupported encodings, and early stream termination return structured errors and close resources.
- JVM and any JS implementation agree on logical schemas and decoded values for their declared common subset.
- Frame core remains free of Parquet implementation dependencies.
set.title: Frame adapter: Parquet source, sink, and truthful pushdown
